newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota targets India market with new India joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Toyota targets India market with new India joint venture.

text.p: Japanese auto giant Toyota Motor Corp said on Monday it hopes to grab a slice of the promising Indian auto market through a joint venture to produce and sell multi-purpose vehicles for large Indian families.
"The Indian market has great potential. At this point, we want to create demand for vehicles designed for large families who carry lots of luggage," a Toyota spokesman said.
Earlier on Monday, Toyota announced it had agreed to set up a joint venture with some companies in the Kirloskar Group, India's leading engineering group.
The carmaker also said it was waiting for approval for the project by the Indian government.
Total investment in the venture, Toyota Kirloskar Ltd, was $170 million, and the company is expected to begin production in end of 1999, Toyota said in a statement.
The spokesman said the names of the companies involved and the breakdown of the stakes held by each party would be released once government approval is attained.
Toyota Kirloskar is the Japanese carmaker's second joint venture in India after light commercial vehicle maker DCM Toyota Ltd.
Toyota sold its stake in DCM Toyota to South Korea's Daewoo Corp in September 1996.

Some analysts say, however, that the type of car Toyota intends to launch would fail to appeal to the Indian community as it would probably be high priced, putting it at a disadvantage against local competitors.

They doubt Toyota would manage to sell more than 20,000 vehicles a year, and said it was highly unlikely that it would be able to grab 20 percent of that market as demand for those types of cars is limited in India.

Japan's Suzuki Motor Corp currently has a market share of more than 70 percent in India's passenger car market, through an equal partnership venture with the Indian government which was launched a decade before the start of economic reforms.
India's passenger car market, opened under a liberalisation programme launched in 1991, has seen the entry of world majors like Ford Motor co, General Motors Corp and Daewoo Corp.
